messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGE fired for P123456 — service: api.redwood.ai, symptom: LB target health degradation + TLS handshake spikes observed in us-west-2. Thresholds crossed for 3m. Auto-escalation -> pagerduty.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered incident P123456 (High) — assigned to: ryan (sre-oncall). Please acknowledge.

ryan (sre-oncall): Acked. seeing 502/504 and TLS errors in frontend logs. pulling metrics and target group status now. @kai can you start with LB target health + DNS checks?

kai (network): on it. trending: target registration churn + some targets reporting TLS handshake failures (ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL). checking host-level CPU and ELB backend health. running dig + curl checks.

emma (infra): throwing up k8s pod health for api-prod: several pods in us-west-2 show readiness toggling. could be upstream connect timeout. past deploy? no deploys in last 30m.

ryan (sre-oncall): copying quick checks — paste these if helpful:
```
# check DNS from public resolver
dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
# attempt TLS handshake verbose
curl -vk https://api.redwood.ai/ --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:52.34.211.100
# ALB describe-target-health (aws cli)
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...
```

kai (network): dig shows multiple A records, but TTLs are low and some entries still returning old IPs from certain resolvers. suspect partial DNS propagation + route weight change earlier. ALB describe-target-health:
```
Target: i-0abc123 healthy: Unhealthy -> reason: Connection timed out
Target: i-0def456 healthy: Unhealthy -> reason: TLS handshake failed
```

lucas (platform): I see an automated rollout to canary nodes 22m ago that should have pinned weights, but rollback didn't complete due to throttling in control plane. I'm re-checking rollout state and will force a rollback if unsafe.

olivia (cs): Getting inbound support tickets: "app shows SSL error" and "can't reach api" from EU customers. approx 18 customers impacted (some 5xx spikes). I'll prepare a short status line if we have ETA.

ryan (sre-oncall): short-running mitigation plan: 1) remove recently-rolled canary from ALB target group (fast failover), 2) pin DNS route weights to previous stable pool, 3) if TLS handshake continues, rotate certs on effected targets as last resort. Kai, can you remove canary targets?

kai (network): removing canary targets now. runner: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn ... --targets Id=i-0abc123`

incident-bot: Action logged: target deregistration requested by kai at 1763000100.

emma (infra): k8s readiness stabilized on remaining pods after canary removal; no new 5xx in internal LB logs for 45s.

ryan (sre-oncall): monitoring for 5m. initiating post-change synthetic: `hey -n 100 -c 10 https://api.redwood.ai/health`

kai (network): DNS weight pin complete. propagation note: some public resolvers will continue to hit old IPs for up to TTL (~90s-5m).

lucas (platform): control plane rollback forced and completed at 1763000300. double-checking config drift.

olivia (cs): updating customers: "We identified an issue affecting connections to api.redwood.ai in us-west-2 and have applied a mitigation. Minimal interruption expected while global DNS caches update. We'll share a postmortem when root cause confirmed."

ryan (sre-oncall): observed drop in TLS handshake errors and 5xx rate returned to baseline ~1763000400. marking incident as mitigated. preparing timeline.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident P123456 acknowledged and marked mitigated by ryan (sre-oncall). Please follow up with RCA and timeline.

emma (infra): saving logs and exporting packet captures from impacted targets for RCA. attaching snippets to the incident doc.

kai (network): preliminary hypothesis: canary nodes had a mismatched TLS config (old cipher suites) and partial DNS weight change caused a traffic split hitting both stable and mismatched targets, amplifying handshake errors. will confirm with cert metadata.

ryan (sre-oncall): next steps: 1) collect full cert/config diff between canary and stable; 2) run regression tests in staging for rollout process; 3) tighten rollout -> require health checks pass for N consecutive checks before changing DNS weights. Assigning owners: kai -> cert diff, lucas -> rollout gating, emma -> logs/pcap.

olivia (cs): thanks. I'll send a follow-up message to affected customers with the mitigation and expected RCA ETA.

ryan (sre-oncall): closing thread once RCA doc link posted. great triage everyone. :thumbsup:
